lines: How fast is a C++ decision engine? Statim hit 68 decisions per second on an RTX 3070.
Laya needs Python and PyTorch, while Statim runs in a tiny binary with no heavy stack.
Statim is a native C++20 engine for System-1 decision models, and it serves Laya-compatible clients without Python.
It merges a native C++ tokenizer with adapted weights so each question becomes one token sequence.
Try it live in a browser with no install, or see this API response decide billing versus technical urgency.
On Ryzen 7 5800X CPU Statim runs at 257 ms per state versus ORT's 266 for short inputs.
Multilingual model accuracy is 0.748 on S1Bench, beating zero-shot Qwen3-8B which scores only 0.706.
It serves many states in a batch without loading extra memory for each adapter.
Statim supports Linux x86-64 CPU and Vulkan, using a single binary plus one GGUF file.
Built by BEKO2210 under Apache-2.0 open source licence.
Linux users download the binary, verify checksums, then run statim serve.
Send this to someone who wants Laya/Jev-compatible decisions with no Python.
Watch Statim answer typed questions with no Python.
